draft.title: Wages and salaries
card: Pay for each hour worked. Weekly wage = hourly rate × hours worked in the week.
A fixed amount for the year, paid in equal instalments. These are often weekly, fortnightly or monthly.
To find one payment from a salary, divide by the number of payments in the year: 52 weeks, 26 fortnights or 12 months.
Example: a salary of $62 400 paid fortnightly gives $62 400 ÷ 26 = $2400 each fortnight. To get a yearly figure from a weekly wage, multiply by 52.
draft.remember: Salary ÷ number of payments gives one payment. Payment × number of payments gives the year.

a.q: Priya earns a salary of $54 600 a year, paid weekly. How much is each weekly payment?
a.why: There are 52 weeks in a year, so $54 600 ÷ 52 = $1050. Dividing by 26 gives $2100, which is a fortnightly payment, not a weekly one.
a.clue: How many weekly payments are there in a year?

b.q: Sam is paid $28 an hour and works 35 hours a week, all year. Pay is the same every week. What is his yearly pay?
b.why: Weekly pay is $28 × 35 = $980. Yearly pay is $980 × 52 = $50 960. The answer $25 480 comes from using 26, which is the number of fortnights, not weeks.
b.clue: Find the weekly pay first, then count the weeks in a year.

check.summary: No problems found. Both answers check out ($54 600 ÷ 52 = $1050; $28 × 35 × 52 = $50 960), and the card stays within the wages and salaries point.
